citation.title: Convolutional LSTM Network: A Machine Learning Approach for Precipitation Nowcasting
citation.authors: Shi, X.; Chen, Z.; Wang, H.; Yeung, D.-Y.; Wong, W.-k.; Woo, W.-c.
citation.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.CV); text indicates NIPS-style submission, venue not confirmed in supplied text

topic: ConvLSTM encoder-forecaster for spatiotemporal sequence forecasting (Moving-MNIST, Hong Kong radar echo nowcasting)
own_question: Can convolutional input-to-state and state-to-state LSTM transitions forecast future radar map sequences better than FC-LSTM and optical-flow ROVER?
actual_method_and_evidence: Uses 5 past radar frames to predict 15 future frames on 97 rainy days (2011-2013). Days are split into blocks assigned randomly. Authors acknowledge same-day train/test dependence. Reports CSI, FAR, POD, MSE and correlation versus ROVER variants and FC-LSTM (Table 2). This is meteorological future-frame prediction, not plasma diagnostics.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Convolutional recurrent architectures have been proposed to model spatially local, temporally evolving fields such as image sequences.
claim_checks.qualification: This is an architectural concept from weather radar and video. It has not been shown for BES/ECEI or CES.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Radar frames every 6 min. The target is future radar frames, i.e. future prediction rather than current-report nowcasting. Arrival latency is not studied.
validation_if_relevant: Random block split within days, with acknowledged dependence. There is no untouched campaign.
forbidden_inferences: ConvLSTM suits BES/ECEI or CES nowcasting
Its 'nowcasting' means estimating a current unavailable report
Its results transfer to fusion plasmas or 10 ms timing
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most, cite this as background on spatiotemporal recurrent models if our estimators use them. The term 'nowcasting' differs from ours, so we should not borrow its framing.
